title: TCP: Conversation Completeness wrong value for some protocols
description:
Some protocols such as FTP might create TCP conversations in
advance before the concerned packets are even parsed. This was
bringing an issue with the completeness value.

Fix #19092

notes.body: mentioned in issue #19092

I think that perhaps the change should go in an `else` to this statement. I believe that if `TCP_S_BASE_SEQ_SET` is not set for this direction that means that the conversation was set up by something else and not processed by TCP. Or the conversation was set up in the opposite direction by a SYN, so that conversation's reverse flow base seq wasn't set, but we already checked for that and created a new conversation.
So if `TCP_S_BASE_SEQ_SET` is not set and we're going to use this conversation anyway and not create a new one, initialize completeness or set the SYNSENT of completeness.
I think that the change as written only has an effect on the second pass (whereas changing it here you could check and only do it on the first pass.)
Absolutely, it's active on the second pass. I am going to see if I can move to the first pass easily and not impacting anything else (that's happening very often when playing with TCP).

I think that if `!(tcpd->fwd->static_flags & TCP_S_BASE_SEQ_SET) && !(tcpd->rev->static_flags & TCP_S_BASE_SEQ_SET)`, then this conversation has definitely not been visited by the TCP dissector before, so it must have been created by another dissector.

The TCP dissector always sets the base sequence number in at least one direction. (Unless `tcpd` is NULL, but that's checked for in the outer if.)

If the fwd direction is not set but the reverse is, that's an extremely unusual case where in the other direction we received a SYN packet, and then, without any more packets on the connection, we received another SYN (not SYN-ACK) in the opposite direction.

That is weird, and should maybe be a new conversation, because the base sequence number will have the first SYN's sequence number instead of the new one's.
Are you talking about the TCP _simultaneous open_ ? I haven't seen anywhere in real life but that should be considered.

That's right, if the fwd base seq is not set but the rev is, and we get a SYN, then it's a rare simultaneous open. I think most of the code works correctly if that happens, with the modified four way handshake, and we don't need to do anything. I reckon I haven't thought about it closely enough to determine if completeness is ok in that case, because I don't have any test captures.
I'll spend some time forging packets then, and see how it behaves.

I added a capture to the issue. The completeness value seems good, however I still wasn't able to send data and we get the _Complete, NO DATA_ .
The _SYN-ACKs_ are marked as _Retransmissions_, maybe should we dedicate an issue to manage this.

Makes sense, proper TCP sequence analysis for simultaneous open should be a different issue. Your sample capture is small enough that once it's fixed it could be added as a unittest too.

Let's just handle the completeness in this issue and MR.
I finally managed to build a similar capture with data (with netcat only it wasn't working, adding a named pipe allowed to inject the data), it was just downloaded in the issue a minute ago.

The _completeness _value seems good for the two _simultaneous open_ captures, as a result of not being very cautious with weird packets (such as the _Christmas Tree_). We could harden this part by adding some complexity but at this moment it looks like nobody is asking for that.
Can we mark this MR as ready ?
